packs.title: What post-training changed inside Qwen 3.5 9B
packs.question: The same question on the 9B model, the base of Microsoft Decision-1: where do base and instruct part ways?
packs.headline: biggest change at layer 29 (52%); one shift vector closes 14% of the KL gap on held-out prompts

claims.text: Post-training moves the residual stream most around layer 29: the median token's state differs from the base model's by 52% of its size there.

Adding one vector, the average tuned-minus-base shift at layer 29 (dose 1; made and chosen on 48 prompts, measured on 48 others), to the base model closes 14% of the next-token KL gap to the tuned model (95% CI 8% to 21%); 8 random vectors of the same size close at most 2%.

packs.title: Where does GPT-2 small notice formal writing?
packs.question: Is formal-versus-casual written in a straight line inside GPT-2 small, from which layer, and how much easier is it to read than truth?
packs.headline: best layer 2: 100% held-out (words alone 100%, shuffled labels at most 71%)

claims.text: The label is linearly readable from the residual stream: at layer 2 a logistic probe gets 100% of 24 held-out examples right (exact 95% interval 85.8% to 100.0%), against 71% at best for probes trained and scored on shuffled labels.
It is readable from the first layer probed (layer 0 of 12).

It is more than the words: a probe on which tokens each text contains, with no model at all, gets 100% of the same held-out examples right (85.8% to 100.0%), against 100% at layer 2 (exact McNemar test on the 0 examples where they disagree: p = 1).
The simple difference-of-means direction at layer 2 gets 100% (85.8% to 100.0%); it is saved for steering, which tests whether the model actually uses it.

packs.title: Does GPT-2 small know which city is in which country?
packs.question: Is "this sentence is true" written in a straight line inside GPT-2 small, and from which layer? (The same test as the Qwen 3.5 2B probe, on a model 16 times smaller.)
packs.headline: best layer 7: 81% held-out (words alone 44%, shuffled labels at most 62%)

claims.text: The label is linearly readable from the residual stream: at layer 7 a logistic probe gets 81% of 100 held-out examples right (exact 95% interval 71.9% to 88.2%), against 62% at best for probes trained and scored on shuffled labels.
It becomes readable by layer 6 of 12: earlier layers do not clear the control.

It is more than the words: a probe on which tokens each text contains, with no model at all, gets 44% of the same held-out examples right (34.1% to 54.3%), against 81% at layer 7 (exact McNemar test on the 47 examples where they disagree: p = 2.5e-08).
The simple difference-of-means direction at layer 7 gets 76% (66.4% to 84.0%); it is saved for steering, which tests whether the model actually uses it.

packs.question: Is "this sentence is true" written in a straight line inside the model, and from which layer?
packs.headline: best layer 10: 99% held-out (words alone 43%, shuffled labels at most 59%)

claims.text: The label is linearly readable from the residual stream: at layer 10 a logistic probe gets 99% of 100 held-out examples right (exact 95% interval 94.6% to 100.0%), against 59% at best for probes trained and scored on shuffled labels.
It becomes readable by layer 2 of 24: earlier layers do not clear the control.

It is more than the words: a probe on which tokens each text contains, with no model at all, gets 43% of the same held-out examples right (33.1% to 53.3%), against 99% at layer 10 (exact McNemar test on the 58 examples where they disagree: p = 4.1e-16).
The simple difference-of-means direction at layer 10 gets 97% (91.5% to 99.4%); it is saved for steering, which tests whether the model actually uses it.

packs.title: A mood dial in GPT-2 small
packs.question: Does one direction, taken from happy-minus-angry sentences, push GPT-2's next word from 'terrible' towards 'great', how much per unit of push, and what does it break?
packs.headline: dose +1 shifts the metric by +7.86; random directions of the same size, at most 2.74

claims.text: Pushing along the direction at layer 6 (dose +1) shifts the metric by +7.86 (95% CI +7.01 to +8.7, over 8 prompts); 32 random directions of the same size shift it by at most 2.74. Loss on neutral text changes by +2.46 nats.

Pushing against the direction at layer 6 (dose -1) shifts the metric by -4.38 (95% CI -5.36 to -3.39, over 8 prompts); 32 random directions of the same size shift it by at most 3.43. Loss on neutral text changes by +2.64 nats.

packs.title: A formality dial in Qwen 3.5 2B
packs.question: Does one direction, taken from formal-minus-casual sentences, turn formality up and down, and what does it cost?
packs.headline: dose +0.6 shifts the metric by +7.31; random directions of the same size, at most 1.54

claims.text: Pushing along the direction at layer 12 (dose +0.6) shifts the metric by +7.31 (95% CI +6.12 to +8.5, over 8 prompts); 32 random directions of the same size shift it by at most 1.54. Loss on neutral text changes by +0.684 nats.

Pushing against the direction at layer 12 (dose -0.6) shifts the metric by -6.44 (95% CI -7.61 to -5.28, over 8 prompts); 32 random directions of the same size shift it by at most 1.59. Loss on neutral text changes by +0.755 nats.

packs.title: Who gets the drink? A feature circuit in Qwen 3.5 2B
packs.question: Which features carry "give it to the other person" (indirect object identification), and do they really matter when patched?
packs.headline: top 100 features carry 90% of the gap on held-out pairs

claims.text: The task works: the model prefers the answer over the foil by +4.81 on clean prompts and +0.15 on corrupt ones (gap 4.67, 95% CI 4.19 to 5.14).

Patching just the top 100 features (of 32768 at each of 5 layers; ranked on 24 pairs and patched on 24 others) to their corrupt values removes 90% of the clean-corrupt gap (95% CI 73% to 109%); 10 sets of 100 random active features remove at most 6%.

packs.title: Thirty-two features from the middle of Qwen 3.5 2B
packs.question: What do a random sample of Qwen-Scope features at layer 12 respond to, and what do they push the model to say?
packs.headline: 32 feature cards at layer 12; dictionary explains 72% of variance here

claims.text: The dictionary reconstructs this model's layer-12 residual stream with 72% of variance explained (cosine 0.89) on 4096 corpus tokens; 1760 of 32768 features never fired on 984141 tokens.
